summary: Bidia Dandaron was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Lubsan Sandan Tsydenov and Andrei Vostrikov. In 1957, he served as a research fellow at the Institute of Mongolian, Buddhist and Tibetan Studies.

Bihani Sarkar works in Indology and religious studies. She held a post at the University of Hamburg and, as attested in 2026, served as Senior Lecturer in Comparative Non-Western Thought at Lancaster University.

Bimal Krishna Matilal was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned degrees from the University of Calcutta and Harvard University (Ph.D. under Daniel H. H. Ingalls), taught at the University of Toronto (~1968–1977), and was Spalding Professor at Oxford (1977–1991).

Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Patna University and SOAS University of London under Lionel David Barnett, later serving as head of department at Patna University (1958) and joint director of K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (~1969–1980).
Bing Chen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He worked as a professor at the Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences (~1981–1987) and Sichuan University (~1987).
Bingtao Ma specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned an MA from Peking University by 2008 and completed a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xue Yu (attested 2015).

Birgit Kellner is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar who earned a doctoral degree from Hiroshima University under Shoryu Katsura. She held positions at Heidelberg University, the University of Vienna, and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Bisheshwar Nath Reu worked in Indology, history, and archaeology after studying under Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha (~1910–1915). He served as Superintendent at Sumer Public Library (~1920–1950) and headed the Sardar Government Museum (~1920–1950) and Maharaja Man Singh Pustak Prakash Research Centre.
Biswajit Biswas works in religious studies and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Rajat Kanti Das and served as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
Biswanath Banerjee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He was on the faculty at Visva-Bharati University from 1967 to 1991 and served as president of The Asiatic Society (~1999–2003).
Bo Jiang specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a PhD from Columbia University, studying under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman.

Bo Utas is an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at Uppsala University (~1961–1972) under Henrik Samuel Nyberg and Stig Wikander, and held a post at Uppsala University from ~1973 to 2003.
Bo-Kwang Han is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Dongguk University (attested 2004 and 2015).
Bokar Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under traditional teacher Kalu Rinpoche (~1960–1989) and was based at Bokar Monastery from ~1984 to 2004.
Bong Seok Joo specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed undergraduate studies at UC Berkeley and earned a PhD from Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser.

Bongkil Chung specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Michigan State University under George C. Kerner and served as a professor of philosophy at Florida International University (1991–1992, attested 2012).

Boris Turayev was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the Faculty of History and Philology of St. Petersburg University (~1887–1891). He taught at Imperial St. Petersburg University (~1896–1914) and Saint Petersburg State University (~1914–1920).

Boris Vladimirovich Semichov was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (~1922–1927) and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1930–1934).

Boris Vladimirtsov studied linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology at St. Petersburg University (~1904–1909) and under Antoine Meillet (~1909–1911). He worked at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (~1911–1931) and the National Library of Russia (1924–1925).

Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima was a scholar of philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Dzogchen Monastery under Thupten Nyendrak, Khenpo Genam, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.
